explanation: Compared against Wikipedia 'Minimal prime (recreational mathematics)' (rev. 1317344170), note to the base-17 count: 'For base 17, there are 1279 known minimal (probable) primes and one unsolved family: F1{9}'. The Lean number 15·17^{k+1} + 17^k + Σ_{i<k} 9·17^i has base-17 digits F, 1, 9^k (checked by decide for k = 3: Nat.digits 17 gives [9, 9, 9, 1, 15]; k = 0 gives 256). IsMinimalPrimeInBase b p := 2 ≤ b ∧ p prime ∧ no prime q ≠ p has its digit list as a sublist of that of p. Sublists of the little-endian digit lists are the subsequences of the usual expansion, and a subsequence with leading zeros contains its canonical form as a further subsequence, so this is the article's definition. Whether some member of the family is a minimal prime is what decides between 1279 and 1280 in the article's base-17 count. @[question] fits. Correct.
